headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP can expose Botpress outputs and secrets if paired without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no documented isolation or provenance controls, and LightAgent can use MCP plus runtime hooks that can observe/replace payloads. If Botpress outputs are routed into LightAgent, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible in the pair, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are forwarded into LightAgent via MCP, stdin/stdout, or a shared workspace
IF LightAgent parses Botpress text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the handoff
Disable automatic tool execution on imported text
Require provenance tags on all Botpress outputs
Review one sample end-to-end message flow
requires-engineering: add schema validation before any agent-to-agent handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, memory, tool results, and secrets, and has broad network egress plus API/MCP surfaces. Botpress has no documented egress and no isolation fields, so if they share a workspace or handoff path, sensitive LightAgent context can leak through Botpress-generated outputs or downstream calls. The default pair is unsafe enough to warrant high severity.
conditions: IF the two agents share a workspace, clipboard, or MCP channel
IF LightAgent processes secrets or tool results while Botpress can read or relay them
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials immediately
Disable sharing of secrets-handling tasks across the pair
Turn off network egress for the LightAgent instance during testing
Inspect logs for any secret-bearing payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while LightAgent can spawn subprocesses, run browsers, use MCP, and supports multiple instances. Those overlapping write-like operational surfaces can conflict if both act on the same mutable resources or environment, even though shared filesystem write is not explicitly documented. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mutable project directory or environment
IF package installation or subprocess actions target shared state without locking
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate container
Avoid shared mutable directories
Serialize any package-install step
Check for concurrent writes during one test run
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent exposes tool calls, tool results, workflow state, and provenance metadata, so it can readily consume Botpress output as authoritative input. Botpress is a customer-support agent that may generate user-facing content; if LightAgent acts on that content without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream actions. The pair lacks documented verification barriers, so high severity is justified.
conditions: IF Botpress output is fed into LightAgent workflows without a human or rule-based verification step
IF LightAgent uses Botpress-generated facts to drive tool calls or workflow state changes
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking
Require citations or source links in Botpress outputs
Limit LightAgent to read-only review mode
Spot-check one workflow for factual drift
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles secrets, user conversations, memory, and trace data, while Botpress is an open-source customer-support agent with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. If the pair processes regulated support data, mismatched retention or residency policies can create compliance gaps. Botpress is cited for the missing controls; LightAgent is cited for the sensitive data classes.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support data is processed through both agents
IF retention, residency, or deletion policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment
Document retention settings for both agents
Restrict regulated data to one agent only
Review logs for residency-sensitive fields
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
